subject: How can I get the the percentage of phenotype variance explained by a QTL?

messages.author: a5ca2a92af41b51f
messages.subject: How can I get the the percentage of phenotype variance explained by a QTL?
parts:
I used scanone() and have caculated several peak LOD markers on corresponding chromosome above the threshold.But some markers nearby the peak marker also have a high LOD value and when I use lodint() it can return a interval including the peak marker,so is this interval represent a QTL?
And as following, is the fitqtl()'s return value "percentage of variance explained (%var)" means the percentage of phenotype variance explained by a QTL? If I only input a peak LOD marker(as shown in the example of the manual),is the %var represent only the peak LOD marker's contribution to the pheno or the interval's mentioned above?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How can I get the the percentage of phenotype variance explained by a QTL?
parts:
Generally, consider a QTL as a single genetic position, but the position is not known precisely and so we use lodint() to derive an interval in which we think the QTL may sit.

The LOD peak is our best estimate for the QTL position, but the QTL is not likely to be exactly there.

The precent variance explained from fitqtl() is an estimate of the percent of the phenotype variance due to the QTL.

karl
